quests.title: Bread for the King's Wake
quests.summary: Half the city is at the Soup Kitchen for the old King's wake. The Square's baker has baked double: three loaves, one each to three mourners at the tables, and no payment taken.

offer.say: #greet#. Half the city's at the Soup Kitchen for the old King's wake, and the Sump's there besides. I've baked double. Three loaves, one each to three wolves at the kitchen tables. Don't let anyone pay you for them. That's the point of a wake.
offer.handIn: The loaves went to the tables.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. He was a good King, or good enough, and he'd have hated a hungry wake. This counter's mine now, and it'll stay in the family. So will the habit of feeding the Sump.

objectives.label: Give a loaf each to three wolves at the Soup Kitchen.
Sit and share a meal at the tables.

quests.title: A Summons to Hillside
quests.summary: The Moot is called, and every farmstead on the old roll gets its summons in writing. The City Office wants Hillside's carried out past Rainmere to the cattle herder.

offer.ask: Is the City Office sending out summonses?
offer.say: #greet#. The Moot's called, and every farmstead on the old roll gets its summons in writing. That's the law, and the law has two paws, both mine. This one's for Hillside, up past Rainmere, to the wolf who herds the cattle. She'll be late to the Moot. They always are.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. One summons served. The law's satisfied, and so am I, nearly. Forty more on my desk. If your paws are good tomorrow, the office stairs are the long ones. I take them two at a time.

objectives.label: Give the summons to the Hillside cattle herder.

quests.title: Stone for the Line
quests.summary: The Line posts out on the roads want four stone apiece. The masons' yard by Northgate can spare two dressed blocks a day: carry them to whichever post you choose and give them in.

offer.ask: Is the yard selling stone for the posts?
offer.say: #greet#. The Line posts out on the roads want four stone apiece, and this yard can spare two dressed blocks a day. Take them to whichever post you like: the Upper Mere, Alder Mere, or our own waystation. I'll write it in the steward's book as wastage.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Two blocks, set where they're wanted. I keep a coal in my pocket for luck, and I've a feeling we'll need it on those roads. Same again tomorrow, if your back holds.

objectives.label: Give the two stones to a Line post.

quests.title: Timber for the Line
quests.summary: No purse in the realm holds timber, and the Line posts want eight or ten poles apiece. The Rainwood woodward cuts two straight poles a day: carry them to a post.

offer.ask: Are those poles for the posts?
offer.say: #greet#. Two poles a day out of the coppice, cut straight, for the Line posts. They want eight or ten apiece, and nobody in this city sells timber. Carry these to whichever post you like. My grandmother cut this coppice, and she'd not have trusted you with an axe.
offer.handIn: The poles are at a post.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Two poles, standing where they're needed. My grandmother would say a post is only as good as the wolf who carried it. She said that about most things.

objectives.label: Give the two poles to a Line post.

quests.title: The Chorus That Sang Wrong
quests.summary: At the howl practice on the Southmeadow square, half the chorus sang the burying howl at a wedding. Two households aren't speaking. The Larkholm lad wants his apology carried.

offer.say: #greet#. We practised the gathering howl on the square, and half the chorus sang the burying one instead. At a wedding. Two households aren't speaking. Take mead to the clay digger's and honey to the carter's, from me, and say sorry ripe and proper.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. They're speaking again, and laughing, which is worse. I've three stories, and that's the best of them now. Sheaf and sickle, never again.

objectives.label: Give the jug of mead to the clay digger's household.
Give the crock of honey to the carter's household.
Win a round at the Vine and Sickle's table, and let the elders laugh about it.

quests.title: Bread for the Bounds
quests.summary: Wolves are walking the old bounds of the cut through the Rainward Hills, long days out on the hills. The Rainward orchard keeper sends bread up for them.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. There's wolves out walking the old bounds of the cut, long days on the hills, and nobody feeds a wolf on a boundary. Three loaves, one each to whoever you meet up on the Rainward Hills. Keep your lamp lit on the high paths.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. I swore at a wedding once to feed whoever came to my door. The bounds are a long way from my door, but an oath runs deep, stone.

objectives.label: Give a loaf each to three wolves out on the Rainward Hills.

quests.title: A Green Stake
quests.summary: Bounders in green have driven stakes into the Oakhaven cut to claim it. Pull one, and take it to the logger at the cut.

objectives.label: Pull a green stake in the Oakhaven cut.
Give it to the logger at the cut.

quests.title: Lamps on the Boardwalk
quests.summary: Lights are walking out on the fen of a night. Fenshore wants its own three boardwalk lamps lit at dusk, so a wolf knows a true light from a false one.

offer.say: #greet#. There's lights walking out on the fen of a night, and nobody wants to follow the wrong one. Light the three boardwalk lamps by the square at dusk, so a wolf knows which lights are ours. Here's oil from the shed. My father did this, and his father before him.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Three lamps lit, and every one of them ours. I'll tell you a story about the marsh lights one day. I've only three stories, mind, and you'll hear all of them twice.

objectives.label: Light the first boardwalk lamp at dusk.
Light the second boardwalk lamp at dusk.
Light the third boardwalk lamp at dusk.

quests.title: Blankets for the Ford
quests.summary: The wolves holding the Larkfield ford sleep out by the water on the siege nights. The Looms have three blankets fit for it.

offer.say: #greet#. The wolves holding the ford sleep out by the water these nights, and the Looms have three blankets fit for it. One each to three wolves at the ford, eh? Full weight, every one. I'd not trust a city carrier with them, but you'll do.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Three warm wolves at the ford. I carve birds while I wait and give every one away; it's the carving I like, not the keeping. I'll have one for you next time. Fair price to you.

objectives.label: Give a blanket each to three wolves at the ford.

quests.title: Benches for the Moot
quests.summary: The Moot sits on Market Square, and every community needs a bench to sit on. The carpenter in the Market Hall wants planks and nails, and dry ones.

offer.say: #greet#. Benches for the Moot, no? Every community gets one to sit on, and the Square's got none. Four planks and a paw of nails, and I'll knock them together. Dry wood, mind. Wet wood makes me cough, and I don't cough.
offer.handIn: Planks and nails for the benches.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Fen-sure, that's a bench a Moot can sit on. The Bright One sees who builds the seats, and so will everyone sitting on them. Dry feet to you.

objectives.label: Bring four planks to the carpenter in the Market Hall.
Bring her a paw of nails.
Be on the Square when the benches go out, between the ninth hour and the tenth.

quests.title: The Coldwater Wagon
quests.summary: Since the paw-mark notices went up, no driver at the Carters' Yard wants the Coldwater road. The carter will drive it if somebody rides with her, or goes ahead and makes the road under Alder Mere safe.

offer.say: #greet#. Not since the paw-mark notices. 'One mark a wagon, paid at the ridge.' I'll drive it. I grew up by the clamps; a lamp on a hill doesn't frighten me. Much. Ride with me, or go ahead and see the road's clear under Alder Mere. Be on the Coldwater square when I come in.

objectives.label: Ride with the wagon, or ride ahead of it.
Get ahead of the wagon to the road under Alder Mere, after dark.
Clear the road under the lamp.
Be on the Coldwater square when the wagon comes in.

quests.title: Before the Black Cloak
quests.summary: Black cloaks came down the Pass and stopped at the Pass House with their boots still on. A Coldwater carter wants the first stage below Frosthollow scouted and cleared before they walk it.

offer.ask: Black cloaks on the Pass, eh?
offer.say: #greet#. Three of them at the Pass House, boots still on. They'll want walking down, and the first stage below Frosthollow is where the Captain's lot sit by the road. Go and look, would you? Clear it if you can, then come and tell me, eh? I've a wagon to drive up there, and I'm fond of my ears.
offer.accept: I'll scout the road below the Pass.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Net and line, I'll hum the whole way up now. Badly. You'll hear me from the mere.

objectives.label: Scout the road below Frosthollow, the first stage down from the Pass.
Clear the stage.
Look in at the Pass House on your way.
Tell the carter what you found.

quests.title: Flour for Larkfield
quests.summary: Larkfield's ovens are short, and the siege has the Downs Road and the fields. Larkholm has flour and nobody to carry it: two measures and two loaves for the Larkfield Bakehouse, up the road or over the downs.

offer.say: #greet#. Short as a sprout. The siege has the Downs Road and their fields both. Two measures of flour and two loaves, counted twice. Get them to the Larkfield Bakehouse. Up the road's quick and watched. Round over the downs is long, and nobody's there. Your choice. Only get there.
offer.accept: Two measures and two loaves, to Larkfield.

objectives.label: Take the road north, or go round over the downs.
Get the sacks through the wolves on the road.
Give the flour to the Larkfield Bakehouse.
Give her the loaves too, before the flour.

bonus.detail: brought Larkholm's last loaves to Larkfield's ovens

quests.title: A Night on the Ice
quests.summary: Since the mere froze, the Larkdowns ewes stand up at night and stare at the ice, and their shepherd swears it rings under them. He can't leave the flock. Sit a night on the Upper Mere shore and listen.

offer.say: #greet#. Since the mere froze. They stand up at night and stare at the ice, eh, and I'd swear it rings under them, low, like a bell. I can't leave the flock. Sit a night on the shore by the Boat Shed and listen for me? Then tell me what it was. Truly, or kindly. I'll know which.
offer.accept: I'll sit a night by the Boat Shed.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Waterlogged, you look. Here's a seat by the fold. They've settled since you came, the daft things.

objectives.label: Wait for the Upper Mere to freeze.
Sit on the shore by the Boat Shed, after dark.
Stay till the small hours.
Tell the shepherd what you heard.

quests.title: The Bell's Felt
quests.summary: The bell goes down to the city for the Moot, wrapped in Coldwater felt. Its weaver wants the felt laid where the cart will stand the night on the stage west of Coldwater, the stage kept till dawn, and the felt brought back to him.

offer.say: #greet#. Every ell of it, and I know the name of every ewe it came off. The bell's cart stands a night on the road west of here. Lay this felt where it'll stand, keep the stage till dawn, then bring it back to me. There's those who'd like it never to reach the city. And I've a question.
offer.accept: I'll lay the felt and keep the stage.
offer.handIn: The stage is kept. Ask your question.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A full net, that. I'll tell the felt it was well laid. It won't answer. Felt never does.

objectives.label: Go to the stage west of Coldwater on the bell's road, after dark.
Drive off whoever wants the stage.
Lay the felt on the road where the cart will stand.
Keep the stage till dawn.
Bring the felt back to the weaver.
He asks whether he should go with it.

quests.title: The Patrolman's Round
quests.summary: The Sump patrolman who keeps the Palace lamp now still walks his round at dusk. After dusk the round is nobody's, and the courts know it. Walk the night half: the four posts, in order, and lend a paw on the way.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The patrolman who walked the Sump round at night keeps the Palace lamp now. He still walks it at dusk, Bright One love him, but after that the round is nobody's, and the courts know it. Walk it for me tonight, all four posts, and lend a paw to anyone who needs one.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Four posts and nobody's purse lifted. That's a better night than the Sump's had since spring. Come back next week. The round doesn't stop needing it.

objectives.label: Walk to the round's first post after dark.
On to the second post.
On to the third post.
And the last, by the wharf stair, before the fourth hour.
Bring down the cutpurses who wait between the posts.

rewards.detail: walked the Sump's night round when nobody else would

quests.title: A Camp Come Back
quests.summary: The camps the realm broke for the Line keep coming back, like weeds in a path. The Watch pays a bounty for any camp broken again on the Line's roads, any of the nine.

offer.ask: Is the Watch paying for camps?
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The camps the realm broke for the Line keep coming back, like weeds in a path. The Watch pays for every one broken again. Any of the nine on the Line's roads will do. Bring down its bandits, break it, and come and tell me which.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. One fewer on the roads. I'd buy you a drink, but the Watch pays me in coal and promises. Take the bounty instead.

objectives.label: Bring down three bandits of a camp on the Line's roads.
Break the camp.

rewards.detail: broke a camp that came back on the Line's roads

quests.title: The Feast Road
quests.summary: Feast days, and half the north walks the north road to Ridgemere's fair, pups and grandmothers and all. Bandits know the feast days too. Walk the road out past the bend and clear whatever is waiting.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Feast days, and half the north comes down this road for the fair, pups and grandmothers and all. Bandits know it as well as I do. Walk the north road out past the bend to where the woods close in, and clear whatever's waiting. I can't leave the gate.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Clear road, full fair. I'll stand here and count them in, and none of them will know your name. That's the job.

objectives.label: Walk the north road from the gate to the bend by day.
Walk on to where the woods close in.
Clear the bandits waiting for fair-goers.

rewards.detail: kept the north road safe for the feast

quests.title: Twelve Bounds in a Day
quests.summary: In the old days the bounds of the Rainward Hills and the cut were walked in a single day, every one, so nobody could say the line had moved. The bounders say it has. Walk all twelve in one day.

offer.ask: You walk these hills a lot?
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The old bounds of these hills were walked in a day, once, every one of them, so nobody could say the line had moved. I petitioned the Council about these hills and lost. Walk all twelve in a day and they'll know it's been done again. Begin wherever you like. Just don't stop.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Twelve in a day. Sheaf and sickle, the Council can keep its papers. The hills have your paw-prints now. Here, the honey's on me.

objectives.label: Begin at any bound of the hills.
Walk all twelve bounds before a day is out.
End at the boundary stone by the Oakhaven cut.

rewards.detail: walked all twelve bounds of the Rainward Hills in a day

quests.title: A Night on the Line
quests.summary: The Moot night is close, and bands test the Line's posts every night to see which ones nobody stands. Pick a post, be there by the twentieth hour and stay till the fifth.

offer.ask: The Watch wants the posts held?
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The Moot night's close, and there are bands testing the Line's posts every night, to see which ones nobody stands. Pick a post. Be there by the twentieth hour and stay till the fifth. If they come, they find you. I'd go myself, but somebody has to cough on the city walls.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A whole night, and the post still standing. Go and sleep. The Line needs you awake on the Moot night more than it needs you now.

objectives.label: Be at a post of the Line by the twentieth hour.
Stand the post through the night.
Drive off the raids.

rewards.detail: stood a night on the Howl Line before the Moot

tests.name: The stage follows the chapters: started, ended, the hourly read, the campaign over
Ch 1-2: wake bread, a summons, the night round walked, one put aside and one run out
Ch 3: stone and timber to the posts, the wagon both ways, and a camp broken at Alder Mere
Ch 4: the chorus mended, the feast road walked by a party, a late wolf turned away
Ch 5-6: bounds bread, a green stake, the fen lamps, the road below the Pass, twelve bounds
Ch 7-8: ford blankets, the haulers fed, flour by road and by downs, a night on the ice
Ch 9: Moot benches, the bell's felt laid and brought back, a party's whole night at a post
